laws.title: Tempo 30 — Berlin's City-Wide Speed Limit Push
laws.subtitle: Berlin has designated hundreds of Tempo 30 zones and seeks blanket 30 km/h limit
laws.fullDescription: Berlin has one of Germany's most extensive networks of Tempo 30 zones (30 km/h speed limits) covering residential streets, school zones, and much of the inner city. The Berlin Senate has repeatedly called for federal law changes to allow cities to set 30 km/h as the default urban speed (currently 50 km/h under StVO). Despite federal resistance, Berlin has implemented over 900 Tempo 30 sections under existing law. Speed cameras (Blitzer) are densely deployed. Exceeding the limit by 21+ km/h results in a driving ban.
laws.penalty: Speeding 1–10 km/h over: €30 fine; 21–30 km/h over: €80 + 1 point; 31+ km/h in 30-zone: licence suspension
exceptions: Emergency vehicles exempt
Temporary Tempo 30 signs around schools and hospitals supersede standing limits
laws.sourceLabel: German Road Traffic Act / Berlin Roads Act

quiz.q: What speed limit does Berlin apply to most residential streets?
quiz.explanation: Berlin has over 900 designated Tempo 30 zones covering residential streets, school areas, and much of the inner city — well above the German average.

laws.title: Mietendeckel / Rent Control Attempts
laws.subtitle: Berlin's rent freeze was struck down by Federal Court; federal rent brake applies
laws.fullDescription: In 2020, Berlin introduced the Mietendeckel (rent cap) — a state law freezing rents and banning increases for 5 years. In April 2021, the Federal Constitutional Court struck it down as unconstitutional (states lack legislative competence over rent). Berlin reverted to the federal Mietpreisbremse (rent brake) limiting new leases to 10% above the local Mietspiegel. Berlin's Mietspiegel (rent index) is disputed — landlords successfully challenged the 2021 simplified Mietspiegel in court. Berlin remains Germany's most contentious rental market with average rents exceeding €16/m².
laws.penalty: Rent brake violation: tenant can reclaim 3 years of excess rent; persistent violations: fines
exceptions: New buildings (post-2014) exempt from federal Mietpreisbremse
Fully modernised apartments may partly be exempt
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Rent Brake Act / Federal Constitutional Court 2021

quiz.q: Why was Berlin's Mietendeckel (rent cap) struck down in 2021?
options: It was too expensive for the state
States lack legislative competence over rent law — only the federal government can regulate it
quiz.explanation: The Federal Constitutional Court ruled in April 2021 that states (Länder) have no legislative competence over rent law — this is reserved for the federal government.

laws.title: Cannabis Consumption Zones — Berlin's Liberal Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Berlin enforces federal CanG but historically takes a liberal approach
laws.fullDescription: Berlin was among Germany's most cannabis-tolerant cities before legalisation. Since the federal Cannabis Act (CanG) took effect in April 2024, adults may possess up to 25g publicly and cultivate up to 3 plants at home. Berlin's Senate declared it would implement CanG fully, in contrast to Bavaria. Cannabis consumption is prohibited within 100m of schools, playgrounds, sports facilities, and pedestrian zones between 07:00–20:00. The Görlitzer Park in Kreuzberg remains a complex enforcement challenge despite police campaigns.
laws.penalty: Possession over 25g: criminal prosecution; consuming in prohibited zone: fines up to €1,000; dealing: up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Cannabis Social Clubs (CSCs) may operate with licence from BfArM
Medical cannabis available on prescription at pharmacies
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Cannabis Act / Berlin General Safety Act

quiz.q: How much cannabis may an adult legally possess in public in Berlin under the 2024 CanG?
quiz.explanation: The 2024 federal Cannabis Act (CanG) allows adults to possess up to 25g of cannabis in public — a limit Berlin enforces without the additional strictness seen in Bavaria.

laws.title: Berliner Mauer — Memorial Protection
laws.subtitle: Remnants of the Berlin Wall are protected monuments; vandalism is criminal
laws.fullDescription: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989. Remaining sections — including the East Side Gallery (1.3km, world's longest open-air gallery) and the Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer (memorial at Bernauer Straße) — are protected under Denkmalschutz (monument protection law, DSchG Bln). Graffiti or damage to protected Wall sections is criminal vandalism (§303 StGB). The East Side Gallery has suffered repeated vandalism despite police protection. The Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer is operated by the Berlin Senate and charges no admission.
laws.penalty: Vandalism to protected monument: fines up to €10,000 and criminal record under §303 StGB; wilful destruction: up to 2 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorised artists may add works to the East Side Gallery under Senate permission
Restoration and conservation work by licensed firms
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Monument Protection Act / German Criminal Code §303

quiz.q: How long is Berlin's East Side Gallery (former Berlin Wall)?
quiz.explanation: The East Side Gallery is 1.3 km long — the world's longest open-air gallery — comprising 105 murals painted on a surviving Berlin Wall section after 1989.

laws.title: Versammlungsfreiheit — Right to Demonstrate
laws.subtitle: Berlin processes thousands of demonstrations per year under strict assembly law
laws.fullDescription: Berlin sees more registered demonstrations than any other German city — over 5,000 per year. The right to assemble (GG Art. 8) is protected but regulated by the Berliner Versammlungsfreiheitsgesetz (VersG Bln 2021). Demonstrations must generally be registered 48 hours in advance. Spontaneous assemblies (Spontanversammlungen) are permitted but must remain peaceful. Police can disperse assemblies only on strict legal grounds. Provocative clothing (e.g., neo-Nazi uniforms) that violates §86a StGB can result in dissolution. Berlin's Polizeiabschnitte use de-escalation protocols.
laws.penalty: Unregistered demonstration blocking traffic: fines; violent conduct: criminal charges; violating dissolution order: up to 1 year imprisonment
exceptions: Spontaneous assemblies in response to breaking news events may require no registration
Individual protest (single person) does not require registration
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Assembly Freedom Act / German Basic Law Art. 8

quiz.q: How far in advance must a demonstration in Berlin generally be registered?
quiz.explanation: Under the Berlin Versammlungsfreiheitsgesetz, demonstrations must generally be registered 48 hours in advance — though spontaneous assemblies are permitted for breaking events.

laws.title: Fahrradstadt Berlin — Cycling Law and Infrastructure
laws.subtitle: Berlin's Mobilitätsgesetz mandates protected cycling infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Mobilitätsgesetz (MobG BE, 2018) — Germany's first state mobility act — legally mandates that the Senate prioritise cycling, public transport, and pedestrians over private car traffic. The law requires construction of 100km of protected cycle lanes per year. Cyclists must use cycle paths where available; helmets are recommended but not mandatory for adults. Cycling on pavements (outside cycle paths) is generally prohibited. E-bikes and e-scooters are regulated under federal law. Cycling under the influence (≥1.6‰ BAC) is a criminal offence.
laws.penalty: Cycling on pavement where prohibited: fines up to €55; cycling drunk (≥1.6‰): criminal charges, licence implications; ignoring red lights: €60–€180
exceptions: Children under 10 may cycle on pavements (accompanied by adult)
Cargo bikes in pedestrian zones with permit
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Mobility Act 2018 / German Road Traffic Act

quiz.q: What did Berlin's landmark 2018 Mobilitätsgesetz legally require?
options: Prioritisation of cycling, public transport and pedestrians over cars
quiz.explanation: Berlin's 2018 Mobilitätsgesetz was Germany's first state mobility law — legally requiring the Senate to prioritise cycling, public transport and pedestrians over private car traffic.

laws.title: Berlin as City-State — Stadtstaatenstatus
laws.subtitle: Berlin is simultaneously a federal state and a city; the Abgeordnetenhaus governs both
laws.fullDescription: Berlin is one of three German city-states (Stadtstaaten) alongside Hamburg and Bremen. It simultaneously functions as a Bundesland (federal state) and a municipality. The Abgeordnetenhaus (House of Representatives) is both the state parliament and the city council, with 159 seats. The Governing Mayor (Regierender Bürgermeister) heads both the state government and the city administration. Berlin has 12 Bezirke (districts), each with a Bezirksamt (district office) and Bezirksverordnetenversammlung (local assembly). Berlin's political situation is complex, with frequent coalition governments.
laws.penalty: N/A — constitutional framework
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Constitution / German Basic Law

quiz.q: What is Berlin's unique constitutional status?
options: A city-state (Stadtstaat) — simultaneously a federal state and a municipality
A federal district like Washington DC
quiz.explanation: Berlin is a Stadtstaat — one of three German city-states (with Hamburg and Bremen) — simultaneously functioning as a Bundesland and a municipality under a single government.

laws.title: Berliner Forsten — Urban Forest Protection
laws.subtitle: Berlin manages 27,000 ha of urban forests; access and protection rules apply
laws.fullDescription: Berlin manages approximately 27,000 hectares of publicly accessible forests and green spaces — an extraordinarily high proportion for a capital city. The Berliner Forsten (forest authority) manages the Grunewald, Tegeler Forst, Köpenicker Forst, and Spandauer Forst. Public access is guaranteed under Berliner Naturschutzgesetz. Cycling, hiking, and nature walks are permitted. Open fires (except in designated grills in designated areas) are prohibited. Illegal fly-tipping in forests is aggressively prosecuted. Tree felling outside the legal period (October 28 – February 28) is restricted.
laws.penalty: Illegal campfire in forest: fines up to €5,000 and liability for fire suppression costs; illegal tree felling: fines up to €50,000
exceptions: Designated BBQ and picnic areas have grilling permits
Forestry operations with prior approval
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Nature Protection Act / Berlin Forest Act

quiz.q: Approximately how many hectares of forests and green spaces does Berlin manage?
quiz.explanation: Berlin manages approximately 27,000 hectares of publicly accessible urban forests — including the Grunewald, Tegeler Forst and Köpenicker Forst.

laws.title: Wohnungslosigkeit — Berlin's Homelessness and Housing First
laws.subtitle: Berlin operates Housing First pilot programmes and emergency shelters
laws.fullDescription: Berlin has Germany's highest visible homelessness rate, with estimates of 15,000–40,000 people without stable housing. The Berlin Senate operates emergency shelters (Übernachtungsstätten) and operates Housing First pilot projects (providing permanent housing without preconditions). The Unterkünfte (facilities) are regulated under AV Wohnen. Aggressive begging (Aggressives Betteln) is prohibited under BerlASOG; simple begging is not illegal. Rough sleeping in parks and public spaces is tolerated unless accompanied by other violations. The Kältehilfe (winter emergency programme) runs from October to April.
laws.penalty: Aggressive begging: fines up to €500; illegal encampments causing sanitation issues: administrative enforcement
exceptions: Passive begging (sitting quietly with a sign) is legal
Kältehilfe shelters are open to all during sub-zero temperatures
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin General Safety Act / Berlin Housing Standards

quiz.q: What does Berlin's Kältehilfe programme provide?
options: Emergency winter shelter from October to April
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Kältehilfe (cold weather emergency) programme runs from October to April, providing emergency overnight shelter for anyone in need during cold weather.

laws.title: DSGVO Enforcement — BlnBDI
laws.subtitle: Berlin's data protection authority (BlnBDI) issues major GDPR fines
laws.fullDescription: The Berliner Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit (BlnBDI) is one of Germany's most active data protection authorities. It issued a €14.5 million fine against the Deutsche Wohnen housing company in 2019 for illegal tenant data storage (upheld on appeal). The BlnBDI enforces GDPR, the Berliner Datenschutzgesetz (BlnDSG), and the IFG (Informationsfreiheitsgesetz — freedom of information). Citizens have the right to request access to personal data held by Berlin public authorities and private companies. Berlin's tech scene (Zalando, HelloFresh, SoundCloud) faces close scrutiny.
laws.penalty: GDPR violations: up to €20 million or 4% of global turnover; freedom of information refusal: appeal mechanism and potential orders
exceptions: Journalistic data processing has wider protections
Academic research with ethics approval has modified rules
laws.sourceLabel: EU GDPR / Berlin Data Protection Act / Berlin FOI Act

quiz.q: What major fine did Berlin's BlnBDI issue in 2019?
options: €1 million fine against a tech startup
€14.5 million fine against Deutsche Wohnen for illegal tenant data storage
€50 million fine against a social media platform
quiz.explanation: The BlnBDI fined Deutsche Wohnen €14.5 million in 2019 for storing tenant personal data illegally without deletion deadlines — one of Germany's largest early GDPR fines.

laws.title: Kunstfreiheit — Berlin's Art and Street Art Culture
laws.subtitle: Street art on public property without permission is vandalism; on private with permission is legal
laws.fullDescription: Berlin is internationally known for its street art culture. Under §303 StGB, graffiti on public property or private property without owner permission is criminal damage. However, Berlin has designated legal graffiti walls (e.g., at Mauerpark, East Side Gallery with permissions), and property owners who invite street artists create legal spaces. The city's Kunstfreiheit (freedom of art, GG Art. 5 para. 3) is a constitutional right. Museum Island (UNESCO World Heritage) is strictly protected. Berlin provides subsidised studio space for artists through the Stadtkulturprogramm.
laws.penalty: Unauthorised graffiti: fines up to €10,000 and criminal charges under §303 StGB; restitution costs added
exceptions: Legal walls and invited artwork on private property — fully legal
Small chalk drawings that wash away in rain not typically prosecuted
laws.source: §303 StGB / GG Art. 5 III / DSchG Bln
laws.sourceLabel: German Criminal Code §303 / Basic Law Art. 5

quiz.q: Is street art on private property in Berlin legal with the owner's permission?
options: Yes — private property owner can invite artists
quiz.explanation: Street art on private property with the property owner's written permission is fully legal in Berlin — §303 StGB only criminalises damage to property without owner consent.

laws.title: Wannsee and Berlin Lakes — Water Quality Law
laws.subtitle: Berlin's 67 lakes are monitored for bathing water quality; pollution is criminal
laws.fullDescription: Berlin has 67 lakes and approximately 180 km of rivers and canals. The Wannsee, Müggelsee, and Tegeler See are major bathing lakes governed by the EU Bathing Water Directive (2006/7/EC) and Berlin's Wassergesetz. Berlin Wasserbetriebe monitors water quality weekly during bathing season. Swimming is permitted only at designated Badestellen (bathing spots) with passing quality ratings. Discharging waste, fuel, or chemicals into Berlin's waterways is criminal (§324 StGB — Gewässerverunreinigung). Motorised private boats are restricted on many lakes.
laws.penalty: Water pollution: up to 5 years imprisonment under §324 StGB; swimming in restricted zones: fines €20–€100; illegal boat: fines
exceptions: Licensed kayaks and non-motorised boats permitted on most waterways
Official water sports clubs with permit
laws.sourceLabel: German Criminal Code §324 / Berlin Water Act / EU Bathing Directive

quiz.q: What is §324 StGB (Gewässerverunreinigung)?
options: The criminal offence of water pollution
quiz.explanation: §324 StGB (Gewässerverunreinigung) makes it a criminal offence to pollute waterways — punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment for serious cases.

laws.title: Zweitwohnungsteuer — Second Home Tax
laws.subtitle: Berlin charges a 15% tax on second homes to combat housing shortages
laws.fullDescription: Berlin levies a Zweitwohnungsteuer (second home tax) of 15% of the annual net cold rent value. This applies to anyone maintaining a second home in Berlin that is not their primary residence. The tax targets investors and those maintaining pied-à-terres. It is one tool among several to return properties to the permanent housing market. Berlin also enforces the Zweckentfremdungsverbot against converting residential properties to tourist lets (Ferienwohnungen) without a permit.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed short-term let (Airbnb-style): fines up to €500,000; non-payment of Zweitwohnungsteuer: back-payment plus interest
exceptions: Primary residences exempt
Students' family homes where they return regularly may be exempt
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Second Home Tax Act / Berlin Housing Misuse Prevention Act

quiz.q: What percentage does Berlin's Zweitwohnungsteuer charge on second homes?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Zweitwohnungsteuer is 15% of the annual net cold rent value — applied to second homes that are not the owner's primary residence.

laws.title: Public Drinking — Berlin's Tolerant Approach
laws.subtitle: Drinking alcohol in public is generally legal in Berlin; designated rules apply in some areas
laws.fullDescription: Unlike many European cities, Berlin has no general ban on drinking alcohol in public spaces. Adults may drink in parks, on public transport platforms (though BVG bylaws prohibit alcohol on the U-Bahn and S-Bahn), and in public squares. However, the Berlin Senate has granted local authorities powers to designate alcohol-free zones (alkoholfreie Zonen) in specific problem areas. Disorderly conduct linked to alcohol is prosecuted under BerlASOG. The Görli (Görlitzer Park) has seen repeated debates about alcohol and drug policy.
laws.penalty: Disorderly conduct while drunk: fines up to €1,000 and removal; alcohol in U/S-Bahn: fines €40–€60
exceptions: Licensed outdoor restaurants and beer gardens can serve on public terraces
Registered cultural and folk festivals operate under event licences
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin General Safety Act / BVG Transport Conditions

quiz.q: Is drinking alcohol in Berlin's public parks generally legal?
options: No — all public drinking is banned
Yes — but not on the U-Bahn or S-Bahn
Yes — everywhere including on the U-Bahn
quiz.explanation: Berlin has no general ban on public drinking — adults may drink in parks and streets. However, BVG bylaws prohibit alcohol on the U-Bahn and S-Bahn.

laws.title: Mindestlohn in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Federal minimum wage (€12.82/hr in 2025) applies; Berlin supplements with sector agreements
laws.fullDescription: The federal Mindestlohn (minimum wage) of €12.82/hour (2025, set by the Mindestlohnkommission) applies throughout Berlin. Berlin also has some of Germany's highest sector-specific collective wage agreements through the DGB unions — particularly in the service sector, retail, and public service (TVöD). Berlin additionally enforces the Vergabegesetz Berlin, which requires companies bidding for public contracts to pay at least the collective sector minimum wage. The Berlin Senate itself is a major employer, bound by the TVöD public service wage scale.
laws.penalty: Paying below minimum wage: back-payment + fines up to €500,000; repeat violations: exclusion from public contracts
exceptions: Apprentices in the first year of training paid at lower statutory rate
Long-term unemployed persons can be paid 80% of minimum wage for first 6 months
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Minimum Wage Act / Berlin Public Procurement Act

quiz.q: What is Germany's federal minimum wage in 2025?
quiz.explanation: Germany's federal Mindestlohn was €12.82 per hour in 2025, set by the independent Mindestlohnkommission and applicable in all states including Berlin.

laws.title: Schulpflicht Berlin — Compulsory Education
laws.subtitle: Berlin enforces compulsory schooling from age 6; home schooling is banned
laws.fullDescription: Berlin strictly enforces the Schulpflicht (compulsory education) from age 6 to 18 (10 years full-time + part-time vocational). Home education (Homeschooling) is prohibited under Berliner Schulgesetz (SchulG Bln). Parents who refuse to send children to school face fines and, in persistent cases, custody proceedings. Berlin has faced high-profile legal battles with Christian families seeking to home-school — German courts have consistently upheld the ban. Berlin's Schulgesetz also governs integration of refugee children, who are entitled to schooling within a short period of arrival.
laws.penalty: Truancy (unexcused absences): fines up to €2,500 against parents; persistent refusal: court orders and potential custody intervention
exceptions: Illness with medical certificate
Approved dual-school vocational programmes
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Schools Act

quiz.q: Is home education (Homeschooling) legal in Berlin?
options: No — it is prohibited under Berliner Schulgesetz
quiz.explanation: Home education is prohibited in Berlin (and all German states) under the Schulgesetz. German courts have consistently upheld this ban, including against families seeking religious exemptions.

laws.title: Charité — University Hospital Law
laws.subtitle: The Charité is Germany's largest university hospital; governed by state and federal law
laws.fullDescription: The Charité — Universitätsmedizin Berlin is jointly operated by the states of Berlin and Brandenburg, and is Germany's largest and most prestigious university hospital with over 100 departments. It is governed by the Berliner Hochschulgesetz (BerlHG) and the Charité-Gesetz. Medical professionals at the Charité are subject to the Berliner Kammergesetz for doctors, pharmacists and other health professions. The Charité played a central role in COVID-19 research, developing the PCR test protocol used globally (Prof. Christian Drosten's team).
laws.penalty: N/A — institutional governance
laws.sourceLabel: Charité Act Berlin / Berlin University Act

quiz.q: What pandemic-related contribution did the Charité's Prof. Drosten's team make?
options: Developed the widely used COVID-19 PCR test protocol
quiz.explanation: Prof. Christian Drosten's team at Berlin's Charité developed the COVID-19 PCR test protocol in January 2020 — which became the global standard for COVID-19 testing.

laws.title: Berliner Polizei — Police Powers and Accountability
laws.subtitle: Berlin's police force is under scrutiny; new accountability laws introduced
laws.fullDescription: The Berliner Polizei (approximately 26,000 officers) operates under the Allgemeines Sicherheits- und Ordnungsgesetz Berlin (ASOG Bln). Following criticism of racial profiling and excessive force, Berlin introduced mandatory police identification numbers (Kennzeichnungspflicht) on uniforms in 2011 — one of the first German states to do so. An independent police complaints mechanism was strengthened in 2021. Anti-discrimination law (Landesantidiskriminierungsgesetz, LADG Bln — 2020) gives individuals the right to sue Berlin state bodies, including police, for discrimination.
laws.penalty: Police misconduct: disciplinary proceedings and criminal charges under StGB; LADG Bln discrimination claims: compensation up to €1,000
exceptions: Police acting under lawful order retain standard defences
Emergency response situations treated with appropriate discretion
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin General Safety Act / Berlin Anti-Discrimination Act 2020

quiz.q: What did Berlin introduce in 2011 regarding police accountability?
options: Mandatory police identification numbers on uniforms
quiz.explanation: Berlin introduced mandatory police identification numbers (Kennzeichnungspflicht) on uniforms in 2011 — one of the first German states to do so, increasing accountability.

laws.title: Berlin Tech Scene — Startup Regulation
laws.subtitle: Berlin is Germany's startup capital; GDPR and employment law apply to all
laws.fullDescription: Berlin hosts Germany's largest startup ecosystem, including Zalando, HelloFresh, Delivery Hero, N26, and hundreds of scale-ups. All Berlin-based companies must comply with: GDPR (enforced by BlnBDI), German employment law (including works councils for companies with 5+ employees under BetrVG), the Mindestlohn, and sector-specific regulations. The Investitionsbank Berlin (IBB) provides startup funding. Berlin's co-working culture and flexible employment (Werkverträge, Freelance) have come under scrutiny for misclassifying employees as contractors.
laws.penalty: Employee misclassification as freelancer: back social security contributions + penalties; GDPR violations: up to €20m fine
exceptions: Genuine sole traders with multiple clients and autonomy can be classified as freelance
Short-term project work under specific conditions may be Werkvertrag
laws.sourceLabel: Works Council Act / Data Protection Act / Social Code §7

quiz.q: Under what threshold of employees must a Berlin company establish a works council (Betriebsrat)?
quiz.explanation: Under BetrVG, employees have the right to elect a works council (Betriebsrat) in any company with 5 or more permanent employees — including Berlin's startups.

laws.title: Museumsinsel — UNESCO World Heritage
laws.subtitle: Berlin's Museum Island is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with strict preservation rules
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Museumsinsel (Museum Island) in the Spree river has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999. It comprises five major museums: the Pergamon Museum, Altes Museum, Neues Museum, Bode-Museum, and Alte Nationalgalerie. The Denkmalpflegeplan strictly governs any alteration to the buildings or surroundings. New construction adjacent to the island must conform to height restrictions and visual integrity requirements. The federal government jointly funds the museums through the Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz (SPK). Admission fees and opening hours are set independently by each museum.
laws.penalty: Construction violating Museum Island visual zone: demolition orders; illegal photography for commercial purposes without licence: civil claims
exceptions: Personal non-commercial photography permitted inside most museums
Restoration and conservation work by SPK-approved firms
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Monument Protection Act / UNESCO World Heritage / SPK Act

quiz.q: Since when is Berlin's Museumsinsel a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Museumsinsel was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999, comprising five world-class museums in the Spree river.

laws.title: Luftqualität — Berlin's Air Quality Rules
laws.subtitle: Berlin implements EU air quality standards; diesel bans in some streets
laws.fullDescription: Berlin must comply with EU Ambient Air Quality Directive (2008/50/EC) limits for NO₂, PM10 and PM2.5. Following court orders by Deutsche Umwelthilfe, Berlin implemented diesel driving bans on specific heavily polluted streets (e.g., sections of Leipziger Straße). The Umweltzone (low-emission zone) covers central Berlin — only vehicles with green environmental sticker (Umweltplakette) may enter. Electric vehicles are exempt from Umweltzone rules. Berlin's Luftreinhalteplan sets annual targets.
laws.penalty: Entering Umweltzone without valid sticker: €80 fine; violating diesel ban on specific roads: €80 fine
exceptions: Electric and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles fully exempt
Emergency vehicles exempt from all restrictions
laws.sourceLabel: EU Air Quality Directive / Federal Emissions Control Ordinance

quiz.q: What is required to drive in Berlin's Umweltzone (low-emission zone)?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Umweltzone (covering central Berlin) requires a green Umweltplakette — vehicles without it or with too high emissions cannot enter legally.

laws.title: Grunderwerbsteuer Berlin — 6% Property Transfer Tax
laws.subtitle: Berlin charges 6% property transfer tax — one of the highest in Germany
laws.fullDescription: Berlin levies Grunderwerbsteuer (property transfer tax) at 6% — among the highest rates in Germany (the maximum is 6.5% in some states). This applies to all real estate purchases and is paid by the buyer. The Berlin Senate has resisted calls to lower the rate, citing ongoing housing revenue needs. Creative deal structures (Share Deals — buying a company that owns property rather than the property directly) have been used to avoid the tax; federal law changes in 2021 tightened Share Deal rules significantly.
laws.penalty: Non-payment: property transfer void; Share Deal abuse: tax evasion prosecution; late payment: interest
exceptions: Family transfers between spouses and direct relatives may be exempt
Social housing transfers under specific programmes may be exempt
laws.sourceLabel: Property Transfer Tax Act / Annual Tax Act 2021

quiz.q: What is Berlin's Grunderwerbsteuer (property transfer tax) rate?
quiz.explanation: Berlin charges 6% Grunderwerbsteuer — among the highest in Germany — applied to all real estate purchases.

laws.title: Sauberkeitsgesetz — Berlin's Anti-Littering Rules
laws.subtitle: Berlin enforces fines for littering; BSR cleans 900 km of streets daily
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Straßenreinigungsgesetz (StrReinG Bln) governs street cleanliness. The Berliner Stadtreinigung (BSR) — one of Europe's largest municipal cleaning companies — cleans approximately 900 km of streets daily. Littering (Wegwerfen von Abfall) is a regulatory offence. Dog owners must clean up after their pets; failure results in fines. Illegal dumping (wildes Kippen) of large items is aggressively prosecuted. Berlin struggles with cleanliness despite significant BSR investment, particularly in tourist areas and parks.
laws.penalty: Littering small items: fines €35–€100; dog fouling: fines up to €100; illegal dumping of large items: fines up to €500
exceptions: Biodegradable food waste dropped accidentally not typically prosecuted
Licensed street markets clean their own pitch areas
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Street Cleaning Act / Circular Economy Act

quiz.q: How many kilometres of streets does Berlin's BSR clean daily?
quiz.explanation: The Berliner Stadtreinigung (BSR) cleans approximately 900 km of streets daily — making it one of Europe's largest municipal cleaning operations.

laws.title: Clubkultur — Berlin's Club Culture Legal Status
laws.subtitle: Berlin clubs are legally recognised as cultural venues with noise protections
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's club culture (Techno, House, Electronic music) is internationally famous. In 2021, Berlin officially recognised clubs as cultural institutions (Kultureinrichtungen) under the Berliner Kulturfördergesetz — giving them access to cultural subsidies and stronger legal standing in noise disputes with neighbouring properties. Berghain's Umsatzsteuerstatus as an art venue (2016 tax court ruling) set a nationwide precedent. Clubs must hold Gaststättenerlaubnis (catering licence) and comply with LärmschutzV (noise protection). Late-night events require special approval.
laws.penalty: Operating without licence: immediate closure; exceeding noise limits: fines up to €50,000; fire safety violations: criminal charges
exceptions: Registered cultural events with Senate support have extended operating permissions
Private members' clubs with selective admission have different licensing needs
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Cultural Funding Act / Catering Licensing Act

quiz.q: What legal status did Berlin grant its clubs in 2021?
quiz.explanation: In 2021, Berlin officially recognised clubs as cultural institutions (Kultureinrichtungen) — giving them access to cultural subsidies and stronger standing in noise disputes.

laws.title: Flüchtlingsrecht — Refugee Law in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Berlin processes asylum seekers under federal law; operates LAGeSo and LABO
laws.fullDescription: Berlin processes asylum applications under federal Asylgesetz through the federal BAMF (Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge). The state's Landesamt für Flüchtlingsangelegenheiten (LAF) manages accommodation. The Landesamt für Bürger- und Ordnungsangelegenheiten (LABO) issues residence permits (Aufenthaltserlaubnis) under the Aufenthaltsgesetz. Berlin has more than 90,000 registered refugees. The state supplemented federal benefits with Berlin-specific programmes. Berlin's LADG (anti-discrimination law) applies to asylum seekers in interactions with state bodies.
laws.penalty: Illegal stay: deportation proceedings; working without permit: fines and permit revocation; employers hiring without checking: fines
exceptions: EU citizens have unrestricted residence and work rights
Convention refugees and those with subsidiary protection have work permit access
laws.sourceLabel: Asylum Act / Residence Act / Berlin Reception Act

quiz.q: Which federal authority handles asylum applications in Germany?
quiz.explanation: The BAMF (Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge) is the federal authority responsible for processing asylum applications throughout Germany, including in Berlin.

laws.title: BVG — Berlin's Public Transport Network
laws.subtitle: U-Bahn, S-Bahn, trams and buses; fare evasion costs €60
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's public transport is operated by BVG (Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe — U-Bahn, buses, trams) and DB Regio (S-Bahn, though under dispute). The network carries approximately 1 billion passengers per year. Fare evasion (Schwarzfahren) costs €60. The €49/€58 Deutschlandticket is valid across all BVG and S-Bahn services. Berlin's U-Bahn has 10 lines and 175 stations. The BVG is a public company (AöR) owned by the Land Berlin. Berlin is the only German city with an extensive inner-city tram network in the western districts.
laws.penalty: Fare evasion: €60 Erhöhtes Beförderungsentgelt; criminal charges for repeat offenders under §265a StGB
exceptions: Children under 6 travel free
Severely disabled persons with pass travel free
€49/58 Deutschlandticket valid on all services
laws.sourceLabel: German Criminal Code §265a / BVG Tariff / Berlin Public Transport Act

quiz.q: How many passengers per year does Berlin's BVG/S-Bahn network carry?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's combined BVG and S-Bahn network carries approximately 1 billion passengers per year, making it one of Europe's busiest urban transport systems.

laws.title: Berliner Verfassung — Berlin's State Constitution
laws.subtitle: Berlin's constitution includes extensive fundamental rights and social state provisions
laws.fullDescription: The Verfassung von Berlin (VvB), adopted in 1995 (replacing the 1950 constitution), contains an extensive catalogue of fundamental rights beyond those in the German Basic Law — including the right to adequate housing (Art. 28), the right to work (Art. 28), and explicit anti-discrimination provisions. Berlin's Verfassungsgerichtshof (VerfGH Bln) enforces the constitution independently. The 2023 Berlin election repeat (ordered by VerfGH due to chaotic conduct of the 2021 election) was a unique constitutional event in German post-war history.
laws.penalty: N/A — constitutional framework
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Constitution 1995

quiz.q: What unusual event did the VerfGH (Berlin Constitutional Court) order in 2023?
options: A repeat election after the chaotic 2021 Berlin election
A referendum on reunification with Brandenburg
A review of all Berlin laws
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Constitutional Court ordered a repeat of the 2021 Berlin state election in 2023 after finding widespread organisational failures — a unique event in German post-war constitutional history.

laws.title: Senatsverwaltungen — Berlin State Administration
laws.subtitle: Berlin's Senate departments are major employers with TVöD wage rules
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's state government is organised into Senatsverwaltungen (Senate departments) covering areas including interior, finance, justice, health, and urban development. The Berlin Senate employs approximately 130,000 public servants (Beamte and Angestellte). Public servants are governed by the Beamtenstatusgesetz (BeamtStG) and Berlin's Landesbeamtengesetz (LBG Bln). Employees in public service receive wages under the TVöD (Tarifvertrag öffentlicher Dienst). Strike rights differ between Beamte (prohibited from striking) and Angestellte (may strike under labour law).
laws.penalty: Beamte on strike: disciplinary proceedings and potential pay reduction; Angestellte striking illegally (outside labour dispute): civil damages
exceptions: Angestellte covered by ver.di collective agreement may strike during contract negotiations
Emergency services have restrictions on strike action
laws.sourceLabel: Civil Servant Status Act / Berlin Civil Servant Act / TVöD

quiz.q: Can Beamte (civil servants) in Berlin legally strike?
options: No — Beamte are prohibited from striking
quiz.explanation: Beamte (civil servants) in Germany — including Berlin — are prohibited from striking under Beamtenrecht. Only Angestellte (public sector employees) retain the right to strike.

laws.title: E-Scooter Regulation in Berlin
laws.subtitle: E-scooters are legal but banned from pavements; helmet recommended
laws.fullDescription: Electric scooters (Elektrokleinstfahrzeuge) are regulated under the federal eKFV (Elektrokleinstfahrzeuge-Verordnung 2019). In Berlin, e-scooters must be ridden on cycle paths or roads — not pavements. A valid driving licence is not required (minimum age 14). Rental e-scooter operators (Tier, Bird, Lime, Voi) must hold city permits from Berlin's Senatsverwaltung für Mobilität and may not park scooters blocking pavements. Berlin has regulated parking zones (Abstellbereiche). Riding drunk (≥1.6‰ BAC) is a criminal offence.
laws.penalty: Riding on pavement: €15–55; parking blocking pavement: fines on operator; drunk riding: criminal charges under StGB
exceptions: Private e-scooters on private property exempt from eKFV
Mobility aids for disabled persons have separate rules
laws.sourceLabel: E-Scooter Ordinance 2019 / Berlin Mobility Act

quiz.q: Where must e-scooters be ridden in Berlin?
options: On cycle paths or roads — not pavements
quiz.explanation: Under the federal eKFV, e-scooters must be ridden on cycle paths where available, or on roads — riding on pavements is prohibited and carries a fine.

laws.title: Berliner Gerichte — Court System
laws.subtitle: Berlin's courts include the Kammergericht — Germany's oldest court of appeal
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's court system includes the Amtsgerichte (district courts, 11 in Berlin), Landgericht Berlin, and the Kammergericht — Germany's oldest and highest-ranking court of appeal (OLG), dating from 1468. The Verwaltungsgericht Berlin handles administrative disputes. The Arbeitsgericht handles employment disputes (important given Berlin's large service sector). Berlin is also home to the Federal Patent Court. Proceedings in civil courts are usually public. Legal aid (Prozesskostenhilfe) is available for those unable to afford legal representation.
laws.penalty: N/A — court system information
laws.sourceLabel: Courts Constitution Act / Civil Procedure Code

quiz.q: What is the Kammergericht?
options: Germany's oldest and most senior court of appeal, based in Berlin since 1468
quiz.explanation: The Kammergericht is Germany's oldest court of appeal (OLG), dating from 1468 and based in Berlin — the highest court in the Land Berlin for civil and criminal appeals.

laws.title: LADG — Berlin's Anti-Discrimination Act
laws.subtitle: Berlin's unique LADG allows individuals to sue state bodies for discrimination
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Landesantidiskriminierungsgesetz (LADG Bln, 2020) is unique in German law — it allows individuals to sue Berlin state authorities (including police, schools, public authorities) for discrimination based on race, gender, disability, religion, age, or sexual orientation. The burden of proof is partially reversed — the authority must show it did not discriminate. Critics argued it would paralyse police operations; supporters say it fills a gap in federal anti-discrimination law which only covers private entities. Berlin's Ombudsstelle (ombudsperson) handles initial complaints.
laws.penalty: Proven discrimination by state body: compensation up to €1,000 per incident; systemic failures: court orders for practice changes
exceptions: Positive discrimination (Fördermaßnahmen) for disadvantaged groups is permitted
Security checks based on objective risk criteria not covered
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Anti-Discrimination Act 2020

quiz.q: What makes Berlin's LADG 2020 unique in German law?
options: It bans all forms of discrimination
It allows individuals to sue Berlin state bodies (including police) for discrimination
It applies to all of Germany
quiz.explanation: The Berlin LADG 2020 is unique because it allows individuals to sue Berlin state authorities — including police and schools — for discrimination, with a partially reversed burden of proof.

laws.title: Rundfunkbeitrag — Broadcasting Fee
laws.subtitle: €18.36/month per household funds ARD/ZDF/BR public broadcasting
laws.fullDescription: All German households must pay the Rundfunkbeitrag (broadcasting fee) of €18.36 per month (2025), regardless of whether they own a TV or radio. The fee funds public broadcasting including ARD, ZDF, and the Rundfunkrat-governed Deutschlandradio. In Berlin, the fee is collected by ARD ZDF Deutschlandradio Beitragsservice. Exemptions apply for recipients of Bürgergeld, BAföG students, and severely disabled persons. The Rundfunkbeitrag is a constitutional matter — the Federal Constitutional Court has confirmed its legality. Non-payment results in debt collection.
laws.penalty: Non-payment: debt collection proceedings; court enforcement; potentially bailiff visits
exceptions: Bürgergeld, Grundsicherung, BAföG recipients: exempt on application
Severely disabled persons (Merkzeichen RF): exempt
laws.sourceLabel: Broadcasting Contribution State Treaty

quiz.q: Who must pay Germany's Rundfunkbeitrag (broadcasting fee)?
options: Only those who watch public television
All households, regardless of whether they own a TV
quiz.explanation: The Rundfunkbeitrag is paid by all households in Germany (€18.36/month in 2025) — the Federal Constitutional Court confirmed it applies regardless of TV or radio ownership.

laws.title: Mängelbeseitigung — Tenant Rights in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Tenants can reduce rent for defects; landlords must repair within reasonable time
laws.fullDescription: Under German BGB (§536), tenants in Berlin have the right to reduce rent (Mietminderung) for significant defects (Mängel) that impair use — such as mould, heating failures, or structural defects. The reduction must be proportionate to the impairment. Landlords must repair defects within a reasonable time after notice (Mängelanzeige). If they fail, tenants can commission repairs themselves and deduct costs. Berlin's Mieterschutzbüros (tenant advisory offices) and the Berliner Mieterverein provide free advice. The Berlin Senate operates a Mietspiegel (rent index) for reference pricing.
laws.penalty: Landlord withholding deposit illegally: civil claim for return + interest; failure to repair after court order: enforcement by bailiff
exceptions: Minor cosmetic issues (small scratches) not grounds for rent reduction
Defects caused by tenant's own negligence not covered
laws.sourceLabel: German Civil Code §536 / Tenancy Law

quiz.q: What right does BGB §536 give Berlin tenants when there are significant defects?
options: The right to move out immediately
The right to reduce rent proportionally (Mietminderung)
The right to claim free repairs from the city
The right to sue the previous tenant
quiz.explanation: BGB §536 gives tenants the right to reduce rent (Mietminderung) proportionally for significant defects like mould, heating failure, or structural problems.

laws.title: Gedenkstätten — Memorial Sites Law
laws.subtitle: Berlin's Holocaust and political memorials are protected and state-funded
laws.fullDescription: Berlin is home to the most significant concentration of German historical memory sites, including the Holocaust Memorial (Denkmal für die ermordeten Juden Europas), the Topographie des Terrors, the Stasi Museum (Stasi-Unterlagen-BStU), the DDR Museum, and over 100 Stolpersteine locations. These are protected under the Gedenkstättenkonzept des Bundes (federal memorial concept) and the Berliner Gedenkstättenkonzept. Trivialisation of the Holocaust (§130 StGB) and denial of Nazi crimes are criminal offences. Memorial sites receive joint federal and state funding.
laws.penalty: Holocaust denial or trivialisation: up to 5 years imprisonment under §130 StGB; Volksverhetzung (incitement): up to 3–5 years
exceptions: Academic historical research and education exempt from §130 where clearly scholarly
Art and satire given wider protection but not unlimited
laws.sourceLabel: German Criminal Code §130 / Federal Memorial Concept

quiz.q: What offence does §130 StGB cover in relation to Berlin's memorial sites?
options: Holocaust denial and incitement — punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment
quiz.explanation: §130 StGB (Volksverhetzung / incitement) criminalises Holocaust denial and trivialisation — punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment — protecting the integrity of Berlin's historical memory.

laws.title: Abfallrecht — Waste Separation in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Berlin requires separation of waste into at least 4 streams; fines for contamination
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetz (KrWG) and Berlin's Abfallentsorgungsvertrag with BSR require households to separate waste into: Restmüll (general waste, black/grey bin), Bioabfall (organic, brown bin), Gelber Sack/Tonne (packaging, yellow), Altpapier (paper, blue bin), and glass by colour (Glascontainer). Contamination of recycling bins (e.g., putting food waste in paper bin) can result in the load being classified as Restmüll at the householder's expense. Berlin achieved 68% separate collection rate in 2024. Illegal dumping is aggressively pursued.
laws.penalty: Contaminating recycling: bin reclassified as Restmüll (higher collection fee); illegal dumping: fines up to €500
exceptions: Small amounts of unavoidable contamination not typically actioned
Medical sharps have separate disposal pathway (Apotheken)
laws.sourceLabel: Circular Economy Act / Berlin Waste Ordinance

quiz.q: How many separate waste streams must Berlin households use?
quiz.explanation: Berlin households must separate waste into at least 4 streams: Restmüll, Bioabfall, Gelber Sack (packaging), and Altpapier — plus colour-sorted glass at street containers.

laws.title: Berlin as Federal Capital
laws.subtitle: Berlin is Germany's federal capital; Bundestag and federal ministries are based here
laws.fullDescription: Berlin became Germany's unified federal capital in 1990 (reunification) and the seat of government in 1999 when the Bundestag moved from Bonn. The Bundestag (German parliament) sits in the Reichstag building. The Bundeskanzleramt (Chancellery), Bundesrat, and most federal ministries are in Berlin. Federal government operations coexist with Berlin state government. The federal government is a major property owner and employer in Berlin. The diplomatic corps (180+ embassies) is based in Berlin. Federal laws override state laws (Art. 31 GG — Bundesrecht bricht Landesrecht).
laws.penalty: N/A — informational
laws.sourceLabel: German Basic Law Art. 22 / Berlin-Federal Capital Agreement

quiz.q: In which year did the Bundestag (German parliament) move from Bonn to Berlin?
quiz.explanation: The Bundestag moved from Bonn to the renovated Reichstag building in Berlin in 1999, completing the transfer of Germany's seat of government following reunification in 1990.

laws.title: Verfassungsschutz Berlin — Domestic Intelligence
laws.subtitle: Berlin's LfV monitors extremist groups; reports annually to Abgeordnetenhaus
laws.fullDescription: The Berliner Landesamt für Verfassungsschutz (LfV Berlin) monitors threats to the constitutional order including far-right extremism (NPD successors, AfD youth in some contexts), Islamist networks, left-wing extremism, and foreign intelligence operations. Berlin is a significant target for espionage given its political importance. The LfV operates under the VSG Bln (Verfassungsschutzgesetz Berlin) with oversight by the Abgeordnetenhaus. Surveillance of individuals requires judicial authorisation. The LfV publishes an annual Verfassungsschutzbericht.
laws.penalty: Membership in banned organisations: up to 3 years imprisonment; espionage: up to 10 years; supporting terrorist organisations: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Academic study of extremist movements is legitimate
Undercover journalism in public interest contexts may be protected
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Domestic Intelligence Act / Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution Act

quiz.q: What does Berlin's Landesamt für Verfassungsschutz (LfV) monitor?
options: Extremist groups and threats to the constitutional order
quiz.explanation: The LfV Berlin monitors far-right extremism, Islamist networks, left-wing extremism, and espionage — reporting annually to the Abgeordnetenhaus under oversight provisions.

laws.title: Pflegegesetz — Long-Term Care in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Federal long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) funds Berlin care homes
laws.fullDescription: Germany's Pflegeversicherung (long-term care insurance, SGB XI) is compulsory for all insured persons and funds in-home and residential care for those assessed as needing it (Pflegegrade 1–5). In Berlin, care homes (Pflegeheime) are licensed by the Heimaufsicht Berlin and subject to regular inspection. The Berliner Alten- und Pflegeheimgesetz (AltPflG Bln) sets quality standards. Berlin supplements federal care with state-funded services for lower-income elderly residents. The Pflegeversicherung covers approximately 60–70% of actual care costs; the remainder is paid by residents or social welfare (Hilfe zur Pflege).
laws.penalty: Unlicensed care home operation: immediate closure and criminal charges; quality standard violations: fines and improvement orders
exceptions: Home care by family members with registered Pflegeperson status receives Pflegegeld (cash benefit)
Palliative and hospice care has modified funding rules
laws.sourceLabel: Social Code XI / Berlin Care Home Act

quiz.q: How many care need grades (Pflegegrade) does Germany's care insurance system have?
quiz.explanation: Germany's long-term care insurance system has 5 Pflegegrade (care need grades 1–5), with higher grades triggering greater insurance payments and care entitlements.

laws.title: Jugendschutz Berlin — Youth Protection Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Berlin enforces federal youth protection strictly at nightclubs and online
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Jugendämter (youth welfare offices) in each district enforce the federal Jugendschutzgesetz (JuSchG) and the JMStV (Jugendmedienschutz-Staatsvertrag). Nightclubs admitting under-18s to events ending after midnight face licence consequences. Alcohol sale to under-16s and spirits to under-18s are prohibited. The 2021 JuSchG reform added online platform obligations — platforms must implement age verification and parental control tools. Berlin's famous nightlife (clubs operating 24/7 on weekends) is subject to strict checks for underage entry, especially at events not classed as cultural.
laws.penalty: Admitting under-18s to age-restricted nightclub events: fines up to €10,000 and licence warning; selling alcohol to minors: fines up to €5,000
exceptions: Clubs with exclusively cultural programming (concerts, art events) may admit minors with parental supervision
Under-16s permitted in beer gardens with parents until 22:00
laws.sourceLabel: Youth Protection Act / Youth Media Treaty / Child and Youth Welfare Act

quiz.q: Under Germany's JuSchG, until what time may under-16s be in a pub or restaurant with their parents?
quiz.explanation: Under JuSchG, children under 16 may be in licensed premises until 22:00 when accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.

laws.title: Hochschulen Berlin — Free Tuition and Student Law
laws.subtitle: Berlin universities charge no tuition fees; students pay semester fees only
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's public universities — Freie Universität Berlin (FU), Humboldt-Universität Berlin (HU), Technische Universität Berlin (TU), and Charité — charge no tuition fees for undergraduate and most postgraduate study. Students pay a semester fee of approximately €300 per semester covering public transport (Semesterticket), student union services, and administration. The Berliner Hochschulgesetz (BerlHG) governs all higher education institutions. Berlin's student population exceeds 200,000. The Studentenwerk manages dormitories (Studierendenwohnheime), cafeterias, and BAföG applications.
laws.penalty: N/A — educational policy
exceptions: Part-time and continuing education programmes may charge fees
Non-EU international students at some institutions pay fees
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin University Act

quiz.q: What is included in Berlin students' semester fee of approximately €300?
options: A Semesterticket (public transport) and student union services
quiz.explanation: Berlin's ~€300 semester fee covers the Semesterticket (valid on BVG and S-Bahn), student union services, and administration — but not tuition, which is free at public universities.

laws.title: Staatsanwaltschaft Berlin — Prosecution Service
laws.subtitle: Berlin's prosecution service handles Germany's highest volume of political crime cases
laws.fullDescription: The Staatsanwaltschaft Berlin (Berlin Public Prosecution Service) is one of Germany's busiest, handling high-profile political, economic, and organised crime cases. It includes the Abteilung für Staatsschutz (state security) which prosecutes terrorism, espionage, and political crimes. Berlin's Abteilung für Wirtschaftsstraftaten handles complex financial crime. The Generalbundesanwalt (Federal Public Prosecutor) based in Karlsruhe takes over cases of national security significance. Berlin's prosecution service coordinates closely with BKA, LKA, and Verfassungsschutz.
laws.penalty: N/A — institutional information
laws.sourceLabel: German Code of Criminal Procedure / Berlin Justice Act

quiz.q: Which Berlin prosecution unit handles terrorism and espionage cases?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Abteilung für Staatsschutz (state security division) within the Staatsanwaltschaft handles terrorism, espionage, and political crime prosecutions.

laws.title: Arbeitsgericht Berlin — Labour Court Caseload
laws.subtitle: Berlin's labour courts handle thousands of unfair dismissal and wage claims
laws.fullDescription: The Arbeitsgericht Berlin (Labour Court) is one of Germany's busiest, reflecting Berlin's large and diverse workforce of approximately 2.1 million. Common cases include: unfair dismissal (Kündigungsschutzklage), wage claims (Lohnklage), temporary employment disputes (Leiharbeit), and discrimination claims under AGG. Germany's labour court system has three levels: Arbeitsgericht, Landesarbeitsgericht (LAG Berlin-Brandenburg), and Bundesarbeitsgericht (BAG) in Erfurt. Legal representation is not mandatory in first-instance labour proceedings. Proceedings are usually concluded within 6–12 months.
laws.penalty: Employer losing unfair dismissal case: reinstatement order or compensation (0.5–1 month salary per service year)
exceptions: Companies with ≤10 employees have KSchG exemption for social selection
Probationary period (6 months) has reduced protection
laws.sourceLabel: Employment Protection Act / Labour Courts Act / General Equal Treatment Act

quiz.q: At which court level are unfair dismissal cases first heard in Berlin?
quiz.explanation: Unfair dismissal (Kündigungsschutzklage) and other employment disputes are first heard at the Arbeitsgericht Berlin — the first instance of Germany's three-tier labour court system.

laws.title: Silvester — New Year's Eve Fireworks Rules
laws.subtitle: Berlin tightened fireworks rules after 2022/23 NYE emergency service attacks
laws.fullDescription: Following the 2022/23 New Year's Eve (Silvester) chaos in Berlin — in which emergency services were attacked with fireworks and dozens of vehicles damaged — Berlin introduced a fireworks ban (Böllerverbot) in 17 pilot zones for 2023/24 and 2024/25. Consumer fireworks (Klasse F2) are legal for purchase only around 28–31 December. Discharge in the no-fireworks zones is prohibited. Rockets and aerial fireworks (Klasse F3/F4) require a professional licence year-round. Police deployed in significantly higher numbers for subsequent Silvester nights.
laws.penalty: Discharging fireworks in banned zones: fines €50–€250; using professional fireworks without licence: fines up to €5,000 and criminal charges
exceptions: Registered professional pyrotechnicians with F3/F4 licence may operate legally
Private gardens in non-banned areas may use consumer F2 fireworks 31 Dec–1 Jan
laws.sourceLabel: Explosives Ordinance / Berlin Safety Act

quiz.q: Why did Berlin introduce fireworks ban zones for New Year's Eve from 2023?
options: After emergency service workers were attacked with fireworks during 2022/23 NYE
To protect the Berlin Wall memorial
Due to noise complaints from tourists
quiz.explanation: After emergency service personnel were attacked with fireworks and dozens of vehicles damaged on 2022/23 NYE in Berlin, the city introduced pilot fireworks-free zones in 17 areas.

laws.title: Flughafen BER — Berlin Brandenburg Airport Law
laws.subtitle: BER replaced Tegel/Schönefeld; strict noise protection zones around airport
laws.fullDescription: Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER), which opened in October 2020 after a decade of delays and cost overruns, is operated by Flughafen Berlin Brandenburg GmbH (FBB), jointly owned by Brandenburg, Berlin, and the federal government. The airport's Planfeststellungsbeschluss (planning approval) established strict Lärmschutzzonen (noise protection zones) requiring building insulation standards. Night flights (22:00–06:00) are restricted. Old Berlin Tegel was closed in November 2020. Schönefeld is integrated as BER Terminal 5. The airport handles approximately 30 million passengers per year.
laws.penalty: Night flight violations by airlines: fines per movement; property construction violating noise zone standards: demolition orders
exceptions: Emergency medical and government flights exempt from night ban
Cargo flights have specific exemptions
laws.sourceLabel: BER Planning Approval / Aviation Act / Aircraft Noise Act

quiz.q: Who jointly owns Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER)?
options: Brandenburg, Berlin, and the federal government
quiz.explanation: BER is jointly owned by the states of Brandenburg and Berlin, and the federal government — through the holding company Flughafen Berlin Brandenburg GmbH (FBB).

laws.title: Landeshaushalt Berlin — State Budget and Debt
laws.subtitle: Berlin has €60bn+ annual budget; federal solidarity transfers support the city
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Landeshaushalt (state budget) exceeds €60 billion for 2024/25, making it Germany's largest state budget by per-capita spending. Berlin receives significant transfers under the Länderfinanzausgleich (fiscal equalisation between rich and poor states) and the Solidarbonus (special federal transfers for structurally weak regions). Berlin's Schuldenbremse (debt brake, GG Art. 109) limits new borrowing. The Rechnungshof Berlin (state audit court) scrutinises all public spending. Berlin's finance senator presents the budget annually to the Abgeordnetenhaus for approval.
laws.penalty: Unauthorised public spending: disciplinary proceedings against officials; fraudulent budget declarations: criminal charges
exceptions: Emergency credit authorisations possible during declared crises (COVID precedent)
Capital investment may be partly exempt from Schuldenbremse calculations
laws.sourceLabel: Basic Law Art. 109 / Berlin Budget Code / Stability Council

quiz.q: What is the Länderfinanzausgleich?
options: Germany's fiscal equalisation system transferring funds from rich to poorer states
A Berlin real estate valuation method
The EU structural fund for Berlin
quiz.explanation: The Länderfinanzausgleich is Germany's fiscal equalisation system — wealthier states (Bayern, Baden-Württemberg, Hessen) transfer funds to poorer states including Berlin to ensure comparable public services.

laws.title: Christopher Street Day — Berlin Pride Law
laws.subtitle: Berlin's CSD is Germany's largest; protected by Versammlungsrecht
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Christopher Street Day (CSD) Pride parade is Germany's largest LGBTQIA+ event, attracting over 500,000 participants annually. It is organised as an official demonstration under the Versammlungsfreiheitsgesetz, giving it constitutional protection. Counter-demonstrations must be separated by police. Hate speech targeting LGBTQIA+ persons is covered by §130 StGB (Volksverhetzung). Berlin's General Equal Treatment Act (AGG) and the LADG Bln prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. Berlin performs same-sex marriages and registered partnerships (federal law since 2017).
laws.penalty: Homophobic hate speech at CSD: potential §130 StGB prosecution; discrimination in access to services: AGG civil claims
exceptions: Religious communities have some exemptions from AGG in personnel decisions
Artistic and satirical expression given wider berth
laws.source: §130 StGB / AGG / LADG Bln / VersG Bln
laws.sourceLabel: German Criminal Code §130 / General Equal Treatment Act / Berlin Anti-Discrimination Act

quiz.q: Approximately how many people attend Berlin's annual CSD (Pride) parade?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's CSD attracts over 500,000 participants annually — making it Germany's largest Pride event and one of the biggest in Europe.

laws.title: Klimaneutrales Berlin 2045 — Climate Neutrality Goal
laws.subtitle: Berlin aims for climate neutrality by 2045 under its Klimaschutz- und Energiewendegesetz
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Klimaschutz- und Energiewendegesetz (KSG Bln, 2016, updated 2023) sets binding targets: 70% CO₂ reduction by 2030 (vs. 1990) and climate neutrality by 2045. The law requires annual monitoring reports to the Abgeordnetenhaus. Berlin's senatsverwaltung für Mobilität und Klimaschutz coordinates the Klimaschutzprogramm covering buildings, transport, energy, and industry. Berlin's building stock is a major challenge — many pre-1970s buildings require deep renovation. The EU Taxonomy and federal BEG renovation subsidy programmes support Berlin's building owners.
laws.penalty: State bodies missing annual targets face public accountability and budget pressures; landlords ignoring energy modernisation notices: court enforcement
exceptions: Heritage-listed buildings may apply for relief from energy modernisation requirements
Extreme energy poverty situations may extend compliance timelines
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Climate Protection Act / Building Energy Act / Federal Renovation Subsidy

quiz.q: By when does Berlin aim to achieve climate neutrality?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's KSG Bln (updated 2023) targets climate neutrality by 2045 — the same year as the federal target — with interim milestones of 70% CO₂ reduction by 2030.

laws.title: Strafverfolgung — Criminal Prosecution in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Berlin has the highest crime reporting rate of any German state
laws.fullDescription: Berlin has the highest absolute volume of reported crimes of any German state (reflecting its large urban population) and one of the highest per-capita rates. The LKA Berlin (Landeskriminalamt) and the Polizei Berlin investigate crimes under the federal StGB (Criminal Code) and StPO (Code of Criminal Procedure). The Staatsanwaltschaft decides on prosecution. Berlin's Strafgerichte (criminal courts) include specialised chambers for organised crime, corruption, and terrorism. The public prosecution acts under the Legalitätsprinzip — it must prosecute all known offences unless specific exemptions apply.
laws.penalty: Penalties vary by offence under StGB; criminal proceedings are public right — prosecution not at victim's discretion alone
exceptions: Antragsdelikte (complaint-required offences) need victim's formal complaint to trigger prosecution
Petty offences (Ordnungswidrigkeiten) prosecuted by administrative authority, not Staatsanwaltschaft
laws.sourceLabel: German Criminal Code / Code of Criminal Procedure / Courts Act

quiz.q: What is the Legalitätsprinzip in German criminal law?
options: The principle that all laws must be fair
The obligation of prosecutors to pursue all known criminal offences
The principle that laws must be written in German
quiz.explanation: The Legalitätsprinzip requires German prosecutors (Staatsanwaltschaft) to pursue all known criminal offences — they have no discretion to decline prosecution based on resources or policy (unlike common law systems).

laws.title: Berliner Außenpolitik — Berlin as Diplomatic Capital
laws.subtitle: 180+ embassies in Berlin; strict diplomatic immunity and protocol rules apply
laws.fullDescription: As Germany's federal capital, Berlin hosts embassies of over 180 countries, making it one of the world's major diplomatic cities. Diplomatic personnel enjoy immunities under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961). The German Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt) is based in Berlin. The city must coordinate security for diplomatic premises and international visits. Diplomatic vehicles may not be ticketed or towed. The Protokollabteilung (protocol department) coordinates high-level state visits. Berlin's Diplomatic Quarter (near the Tiergarten) has distinct architectural planning rules.
laws.penalty: Interfering with diplomatic premises: criminal charges under §102 StGB (Verletzung ausländischer Gebietshoheit)
exceptions: Diplomatic immunity covers most civil and criminal matters for accredited diplomats
Administrative staff have partial immunity
laws.sourceLabel: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations / German Criminal Code §102

quiz.q: How many country embassies are based in Berlin?
quiz.explanation: Berlin hosts embassies of over 180 countries — making it one of the world's busiest diplomatic capitals — with diplomatic personnel protected by the 1961 Vienna Convention.

laws.title: Behindertenrecht — Disability Rights in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Berlin's LADG and federal BTHG protect disabled persons' equal participation
laws.fullDescription: Disability rights in Berlin are governed by the federal Bundesteilhabegesetz (BTHG, 2018) ensuring 'Teilhabe' (participation) in all areas of life, and Berlin's own LADG (anti-discrimination law). The Landesbeauftragter für Menschen mit Behinderungen monitors compliance. Public buildings and transport must be progressively made accessible under the Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz (BGG). BVG's U-Bahn network is approximately 95% step-free accessible. The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD, 2006) applies directly in Germany. Workplace discrimination based on disability violates the AGG.
laws.penalty: Workplace disability discrimination: AGG compensation claims; public building accessibility violations: administrative enforcement
exceptions: Small businesses and historical buildings may have extended accessibility compliance periods
Private residential properties are generally exempt from public accessibility mandates
laws.source: BTHG / BGG / AGG / LADG Bln / UN-BRK
laws.sourceLabel: Participation Strengthening Act / Disability Equality Act / UN CRPD

quiz.q: What does Germany's BTHG (Bundesteilhabegesetz) ensure for disabled persons?
options: Full participation (Teilhabe) in all areas of life
quiz.explanation: The BTHG (2018) — Bundesteilhabegesetz — ensures Teilhabe (full participation) for disabled persons in employment, housing, education and social life, replacing the older welfare model with a rights-based approach.

laws.title: Berlinale — International Film Festival Law
laws.subtitle: The Berlinale is one of the world's top film festivals; operates under event licensing
laws.fullDescription: The Berlinale (Berlin International Film Festival) is held annually in February and is one of the world's Big Three film festivals alongside Cannes and Venice. It is organised by the Internationale Filmfestspiele Berlin GmbH, a company under federal and state oversight. The festival operates under comprehensive event licences from Berlin's Ordnungsamt. Films screened must comply with FSK age ratings. The Golden Bear (Goldener Bär) jury selects winners independently. The Berlinale attracts approximately 350,000 visitors and 4,500 press accreditations annually.
laws.penalty: Screening age-restricted films without adequate age control: fines; unlicensed event operation: immediate closure
exceptions: Press screenings and industry events may have modified age requirements
Films under 5 minutes or non-narrative works may have simplified rating requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Youth Protection Act / Catering Act / FSK Film Rating Rules

quiz.q: What award does the Berlinale give to the best film?
quiz.explanation: The Berlinale's top award is the Golden Bear (Goldener Bär) — one of cinema's most prestigious prizes, alongside Cannes' Palme d'Or and Venice's Golden Lion.

laws.title: Lärmschutz — Noise Protection in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Strict noise limits protect residents; construction noise regulated by timetables
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Lärmschutz (noise protection) is governed by the federal TA Lärm (Technical Instructions on Noise), the 16. BImSchV (noise protection for transport infrastructure), and Berlin's own LärmschutzV. Residential areas have limits of 55 dB(A) day and 40 dB(A) night. Construction noise is permitted Monday–Saturday 07:00–20:00. Sunday construction is prohibited except in genuine emergencies. Music from clubs, bars, and events must comply with the TA Lärm. Berlin's noise map (Lärmkartierung) identifies hotspots for policy measures.
laws.penalty: Exceeding permitted noise levels: fines up to €50,000; persistent violations: operational closure; illegal night construction: criminal liability
exceptions: Essential public works (emergency repair) may proceed at night with authority approval
Agricultural machinery in rural zones may operate outside standard hours in harvest season
laws.sourceLabel: Technical Noise Instructions / Federal Emissions Control Ordinance 16

quiz.q: What is the maximum permitted noise level in Berlin residential areas at night?
quiz.explanation: Berlin residential areas are limited to 40 dB(A) at night — equivalent to a quiet library — enforced under the TA Lärm and Berlin's Lärmschutzverordnung.

laws.title: Rettungsdienst — Emergency Medical Services
laws.subtitle: Berlin's fire brigade (Feuerwehr) operates combined emergency ambulance service
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Feuerwehr (fire brigade) and Berliner Feuerwehr GmbH operate the Rettungsdienst (emergency medical services) under the Berliner Rettungsdienstgesetz (BerlRDG). The European emergency number 112 connects to coordinated EMS/fire dispatch. Deliberately blocking emergency vehicles or the Rettungsgasse (emergency lane on motorways) is a criminal offence. Response time targets are set in the BerlRDG. Berlin's Rettungsdienst handles approximately 600,000 emergency calls per year. First aid training is not legally mandatory for private individuals but is required for driving licence applicants.
laws.penalty: Blocking emergency vehicles: fines up to €240 and points; failing to form Rettungsgasse: fines up to €320 + 2 points; obstruction causing injury: criminal charges
exceptions: Road users in gridlock who physically cannot move are not liable
Pedestrians crossing safely are not required to actively assist
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Emergency Services Act / German Road Traffic Act §38

quiz.q: What is the Rettungsgasse?
options: A bicycle lane for emergency use
The emergency corridor that drivers must form on motorways for rescue vehicles
A lane reserved for police cars
quiz.explanation: The Rettungsgasse is the emergency corridor motorway drivers must create by moving to the sides — left lane to left, all others to the right — to allow emergency vehicles through.

laws.title: Kleingärten — Berlin's Allotment Garden Law
laws.subtitle: Berlin has 70,000 allotment gardens governed by the Bundeskleingartengesetz
laws.fullDescription: Berlin has approximately 70,000 Kleingärten (allotment gardens) across 900 sites — more than any other German city. They are governed by the federal Bundeskleingartengesetz (BKleingG), which limits garden plots to 400 m², requires at least one third to be used for food production, and restricts structures to non-habitable garden sheds (Lauben) of maximum 24 m². Permanent residence in a Kleingartenanlage is prohibited. Rents are heavily subsidised. Berlin's Kleingärten are under pressure from development interests; significant legal protections exist against their abolition.
laws.penalty: Using Kleingartenlaube as permanent residence: eviction and fines; exceeding 24 m² structure: demolition order
exceptions: Registered disabled gardeners may have adapted access structures
Temporary extended stays during gardening season are tolerated
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Allotment Garden Act / Berlin District Government Act

quiz.q: What is the maximum size of a Kleingartenlaube (allotment shed) in Berlin?
quiz.explanation: Under the Bundeskleingartengesetz, Kleingarten sheds (Lauben) may not exceed 24 m² and must not be habitable as permanent residences.

laws.title: Parkraum Berlin — Parking Law and Zones
laws.subtitle: Berlin extends paid parking zones; illegal parking on cycle paths carries heavy fines
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Parkraum management is handled by the Bezirke (districts). The city has steadily expanded Bewohnerparkzonen (resident parking zones) requiring permits for locals and parking meters for visitors. Illegal parking on cycle paths (Radwege) carries a €55 fine — higher than many other cities due to safety concerns. Double parking is vigorously enforced. Berlin has introduced some car-free streets and broadened pedestrian zones. Parking meter revenues fund public transport improvements. The Parkausweis (parking permit) costs approximately €10/year for residents.
laws.penalty: Parking on cycle path: €55 fine; blocking fire brigade access: vehicle towing + fines up to €250; parking without valid permit in Bewohnerparkzone: €25
exceptions: Loading/unloading deliveries: generally up to 3 minutes permitted with hazard lights
Disabled persons with Parkausweis for disabled have extended rights
laws.sourceLabel: German Road Traffic Act / Berlin Roads Act / District Parking Ordinance

quiz.q: What fine does Berlin impose for parking illegally on a cycle path?
quiz.explanation: Berlin charges €55 for illegal parking on a cycle path (Radweg) — higher than many cities — reflecting the safety risk to cyclists from blocked cycling infrastructure.

laws.title: Vertragsrecht — Contract Law in Berlin
laws.subtitle: German BGB governs all contracts; consumer protections are strong
laws.fullDescription: All contracts in Berlin are governed by the federal Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch (BGB). Consumers (Verbraucher) have a statutory 14-day right of withdrawal (Widerrufsrecht) for distance contracts (online shopping, telephone sales) and door-to-door sales under §312g BGB. The Verbraucherzentrale Berlin provides free advice on consumer rights. Standard contract terms (AGB) that are unreasonably disadvantageous to consumers are void under §307 BGB. Berlin's Amtsgericht Mitte handles small claims (Mahnbescheid) for amounts under €5,000. The European Small Claims Procedure applies for EU cross-border disputes.
laws.penalty: Refusing to honour statutory Widerrufsrecht: civil liability for refund; AGB violations: injunctions from Verbraucherzentrale
exceptions: Custom-made goods exempt from Widerrufsrecht
Perishable goods and digital content after download commencement may be exempt
laws.sourceLabel: German Civil Code §312g / EU Consumer Rights Directive

quiz.q: How many days does a German consumer have to withdraw from an online purchase?
quiz.explanation: Under BGB §312g and the EU Consumer Rights Directive, German consumers have a 14-day Widerrufsrecht (right of withdrawal) for online and telephone purchases.

laws.title: Gewerbesteuer — Berlin's Trade Tax
laws.subtitle: Berlin levies Gewerbesteuer at 410% assessment rate on business profits
laws.fullDescription: Berlin levies Gewerbesteuer (trade tax) at a Hebesatz (assessment rate) of 410% on business profits — above the German average but lower than Munich (490%) and Frankfurt (460%). The trade tax base is calculated on profits with various adjustments (Hinzurechnungen und Kürzungen). Sole traders and partnerships with profits under €24,500/year are exempt. Gewerbesteuer funds a significant portion of Berlin's budget. Berlin's corporate tax environment (combining federal Körperschaftsteuer 15% + Solidaritätszuschlag + Gewerbesteuer) results in an effective rate of approximately 30%.
laws.penalty: Non-payment: interest and enforcement by Finanzamt; tax fraud: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Freelancers (Freiberufler — doctors, lawyers, artists) are exempt from Gewerbesteuer
Non-profit organisations (gemeinnützige Vereine) generally exempt
laws.sourceLabel: German Trade Tax Act / Trade Tax Guidelines

quiz.q: What is Berlin's Gewerbesteuer Hebesatz (assessment rate)?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Gewerbesteuer Hebesatz is 410% — above the German average but below major cities like Munich (490%). Freelancers and non-profits are exempt.

laws.title: Bibliotheksrecht — Berlin's Library System
laws.subtitle: Berlin's 80+ public libraries are governed by the Bibliotheksgesetz Berlin
Berlin's public library law guarantees free access to knowledge
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Bibliotheksgesetz Berlin (BiblG Bln, 2021) — one of Germany's few state-level library laws — guarantees free access to Berlin's public library network, including the Zentral- und Landesbibliothek (ZLB), 80+ district library branches, and digital resources. Library use is free of charge for residents under the BiblG Bln. Copyright law (UrhG) governs which works may be digitised and lent. The Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz (SPK) manages major Berlin collections including the Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin (two locations). Berlin libraries lend approximately 10 million items annually.
laws.penalty: Non-return of library items: fines up to €30 per item; wilful damage to library property: civil liability + potential criminal damage charges
exceptions: Short-term reference materials must be used in-library only
Digital loans expire automatically — no return required
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Library Act 2021 / German Copyright Act

quiz.q: What did Berlin's BiblG Bln (2021) introduce?
options: A legal guarantee of free public library access for Berlin residents
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Bibliotheksgesetz (2021) — one of Germany's first state library laws — legally guarantees free access to public library services for all Berlin residents.
