laws.title: Elterngeld und Elternzeit — Parental Leave in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Federal Elterngeld pays up to €1,800/month; Elternzeit protects job for 3 years
laws.fullDescription: Federal Bundeselterngeld- und Elternzeitgesetz (BEEG) entitles parents to Elterngeld (parental benefit) of 65–67% of pre-birth net income (up to €1,800/month) for up to 14 months (or 28 months for Elterngeld Plus at half the rate). Elternzeit (parental leave) protects the employment contract for up to 3 years per child. Both parents can take leave simultaneously or consecutively. Berlin's major employers — public sector, tech, media — generally support flexible return-to-work arrangements. The Berlin Senate operates a Väternetzwerk (fathers' network) promoting shared parental leave.
laws.penalty: Employer refusing to grant statutory Elternzeit: court enforcement and potential damages; wrongful dismissal during Elternzeit: reinstatement order
exceptions: Self-employed persons may claim Elterngeld but have no employer to grant Elternzeit
Adoption and foster parents have equivalent rights
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Parental Benefit and Leave Act

quiz.q: How long does Elternzeit (parental leave job protection) last per child in Germany?
quiz.explanation: Under BEEG, Elternzeit protects the employment contract for up to 3 years per child — both parents may take it, simultaneously or consecutively.

laws.title: Bundestagswahlrecht — Federal Election Law in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Berlin elects 28 Bundestag members across 12 constituencies
laws.fullDescription: Berlin elects 28 Bundestag members across 12 Wahlkreise (constituencies) at federal elections held every 4 years. The mixed-member proportional representation system (Personalisiertes Verhältniswahlrecht) gives each voter two votes: Erststimme (direct candidate) and Zweitstimme (party list). The Bundeswahlgesetz reformed in 2023 reduced the Bundestag from 736 to approximately 630 seats. Berlin is also home to the Bundeswahlleiter (Federal Returning Officer) who administers federal elections. Berlin's chaotic 2021 election — with polling station failures and wrong ballot papers — led to the VerfGH ordering a partial repeat.
laws.penalty: Electoral fraud: up to 5 years imprisonment under §107 StGB; buying votes: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Spoiled ballots counted and published but not valid votes
Overseas Germans may vote by postal ballot
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Electoral Act / German Criminal Code §107

quiz.q: How many Berlin constituencies elect members directly to the Bundestag?
quiz.explanation: Berlin has 12 Wahlkreise (constituencies) each directly electing one Bundestag member by Erststimme, plus proportional seats allocated by Zweitstimme party vote.

laws.title: Bauordnung Berlin — Building Regulations
laws.subtitle: All construction in Berlin requires a Baugenehmigung; strict height and design rules apply
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Bauordnung Berlin (BauOBln) requires a Baugenehmigung (building permit) for virtually all new construction, major alterations, and change of use. Applications go to the Bezirksbauamt. Berlin has specific Bebauungspläne (development plans) for each area setting permissible uses, heights, and densities. Historic central Berlin has strict height limits (generally 22m — the 'Traufhöhe' cornice line established under urban planning rules). The Senatsverwaltung für Stadtentwicklung oversees major projects. Unauthorised construction can result in demolition orders enforceable by the state.
laws.penalty: Construction without permit: stop-work order and fines up to €500,000; persistent violation: demolition at owner's expense
exceptions: Minor garden structures under 10 m³ may not require full permit in some Bezirke
Emergency structural repairs may begin without prior approval if reported immediately
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Building Code / Federal Building Code

quiz.q: What traditional height limit applies in much of central Berlin?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's traditional Traufhöhe (cornice height) of approximately 22 m has shaped the city's skyline — maintaining the typical 6–7 storey profile of Gründerzeit blocks in central districts.

laws.title: §86a StGB — Banned Symbols Law
laws.subtitle: Nazi symbols, SS insignia, and other banned organisation symbols are criminal in Berlin
laws.fullDescription: §86a StGB prohibits the public display, distribution, or use of symbols of unconstitutional organisations in Germany — including the swastika, SS runes, Heil Hitler salute, and other Nazi insignia. Berlin, as a city with major Holocaust memorial sites and large tourist numbers, enforces §86a strictly. Displaying such symbols — even as a costume or in a photograph — can result in criminal charges. The law also covers symbols of other banned organisations (certain Islamist groups, PKK). Art, academic research, and clearly counter-cultural antifascist use are exempt under the 'Sozialadäquanzklausel'.
laws.penalty: Displaying banned symbols: up to 3 years imprisonment or fines under §86a StGB; commercial production/distribution: higher penalties
exceptions: Academic study, journalism, and artistic use (where clearly antifascist or educational) exempt under §86a(3)
Historical documentation and museum display exempt
laws.sourceLabel: German Criminal Code §86a

quiz.q: Can displaying a swastika in Berlin ever be legal?
options: Yes — in academic, journalistic, artistic or antifascist contexts under §86a(3)
quiz.explanation: §86a(3) contains a Sozialadäquanzklausel — academic, journalistic, artistic, and clearly antifascist uses are exempt from the symbol ban, though the line is drawn strictly by courts.

laws.title: Kita-Gesetz — Childcare Law in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Berlin provides free Kita (nursery) places from age 1; mandatory school readiness
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Kindertagesförderungsgesetz (KitaFöG Bln) guarantees a Kita (Kindertagesstätte/nursery) place for every child from age 1 to school entry. Since 2018, Kita places in Berlin are free of charge (Beitragsfreiheit) regardless of parental income. Children must attend a school readiness assessment (Sprachstandsfeststellung) before school entry. Berlin has invested heavily in Kita expansion to meet demand. Kita staff ratios are regulated under the KitaFöG. Berlin's Qualitätsentwicklung programme aims to raise standards across the approximately 2,500 Kita facilities.
laws.penalty: Kita operators violating staff ratio requirements: warning and licence suspension; failure to report safeguarding concerns: disciplinary action
exceptions: Tagespflegepersonen (childminders) operate under simplified registration not full Kita rules
Religious community Kitas may maintain denominational character within regulated framework
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Childcare Promotion Act

quiz.q: Since when are Kita (nursery) places in Berlin free of charge?
quiz.explanation: Berlin introduced free Kita places (Beitragsfreiheit) for all children from age 1 to school entry in 2018 — regardless of parental income — a landmark social policy.

laws.title: Staatliche Museen — National Museum Law
laws.subtitle: Berlin's 17 Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz museums are federal cultural assets
laws.fullDescription: The Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz (SPK) manages 17 Berlin museums including the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, the Staatsbibliothek, and the Geheimes Staatsarchiv. The SPK is a federal foundation jointly funded by the federal government (75%) and the 16 German states (25%). SPK collections total approximately 5 million objects. Provenance research (Provenienzforschung) to identify Nazi-looted art is legally mandated under the Washington Principles (1998) and Magdeburg Guidelines (1999). Restitution of proven Nazi-looted art is legally required.
laws.penalty: Failure to conduct provenance research as required: reputational and diplomatic sanctions; non-restitution of proven looted art: international legal proceedings
exceptions: Wartime losses through bombing or Soviet trophy removal have different legal status from Nazi looting
Statute of limitations issues may affect older claims in some cases
laws.sourceLabel: SPK Act / Washington Principles / Cultural Property Return Act

quiz.q: What does Nazi-looted art provenance research (Provenienzforschung) legally require SPK museums to do?
options: Identify and return (restitute) proven Nazi-looted works to rightful heirs
Destroy all artwork of unclear origin
Transfer items to federal government ownership
quiz.explanation: Under the Washington Principles and German KulturGutRückG, SPK museums must conduct provenance research and restitute proven Nazi-looted art to rightful owners or their heirs.

laws.title: Tierschutz in Berlin — Urban Wildlife Protection
laws.subtitle: Feeding pigeons is prohibited in some areas; injured wildlife must be reported
laws.fullDescription: Urban wildlife in Berlin is governed by the Tierschutzgesetz (TierSchG) and Berlin's NatSchGBln. Intentional killing or injuring of wild birds (including pigeons) is prohibited under §44 BNatSchG. In some Berlin districts, an Fütterungsverbot (feeding prohibition) for pigeons exists in designated areas to reduce pest populations and health risks. Finding an injured wild animal creates a de facto duty to report or assist; the Wildtiertelefon (wildlife hotline) operated by the Tierärztekammer Berlin is the contact point. Urban fox populations in Berlin are protected but may be controlled by licensed hunters in designated areas.
laws.penalty: Killing protected wild birds: fines up to €65,000 or criminal charges; feeding pigeons in prohibited zones: fines up to €500
exceptions: Pest control of listed species (rats, mice) by licensed operators permitted
Licensed hunters managing fox populations in designated Berlin areas
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Nature Protection Act §44 / Animal Welfare Act

quiz.q: Is it legal to feed pigeons in all areas of Berlin?
options: No — feeding prohibitions exist in designated areas of some districts
quiz.explanation: Some Berlin districts have designated Fütterungsverbotszonen (pigeon feeding prohibition areas) to control pest populations — breaking these rules carries fines up to €500.

laws.title: Finanzamt Berlin — Tax Administration
laws.subtitle: Berlin has 8 Finanzämter; income tax (EStG) and corporate tax (KStG) apply
laws.fullDescription: Berlin operates 8 Finanzämter (tax offices) divided by district. All residents and businesses must register with the relevant Finanzamt. Individual income tax (Einkommensteuer, EStG) applies to worldwide income for German tax residents; rates are 14–45% with Soli. The Kirchensteuer (8% in Berlin, collected by Finanzamt) applies to registered church members. Annual Steuererklärung (tax return) must be filed by 31 July (or 28 February with a Steuerberater). Self-employed persons pay quarterly advance tax (Vorauszahlung). Tax evasion (Steuerhinterziehung, §370 AO) is a criminal offence.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: up to 10 years imprisonment for serious cases under §370 AO; late filing: automatic Verspätungszuschlag (late penalty); non-payment: Mahnbescheid and enforcement
exceptions: Pensioners below the Grundfreibetrag (€11,604 in 2024) may not need to file
Steuerberater-assisted returns have extended filing deadlines
laws.sourceLabel: Income Tax Act / Corporate Tax Act / Tax Code §370

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for serious tax evasion (§370 AO) in Germany?
quiz.explanation: §370 AO (Steuerhinterziehung) carries up to 10 years imprisonment for particularly serious tax evasion — for example large-scale systematic fraud or use of fictitious transactions.

laws.title: Hundegesetz — Berlin's Dog Law
laws.subtitle: Dangerous dog breeds require liability insurance; all dogs need registration
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Hundegesetz (HundeG Bln) requires all dog owners to register their dogs with the Ordnungsamt and pay the Hundesteuer (dog tax — approximately €120/year per dog in Berlin, one of Germany's highest). Dogs must be kept on a lead in most public areas. Certain breeds classified as 'gefährliche Hunde' (dangerous dogs — including Pit Bull Terriers, American Staffordshire Terriers, Staffordshire Bull Terriers, and Bull Terriers) require additional liability insurance (minimum €1 million) and a Wesenstest (temperament test). Muzzles are required for dangerous breeds in public.
laws.penalty: Unregistered dog: fines up to €2,500; dangerous breed without insurance or muzzle: fines up to €10,000; dog causing injury: civil liability on owner
exceptions: Service and guide dogs (Blindenführhunde) exempt from lead and muzzle requirements
Police dogs exempt during operational use
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Dog Act / Animal Welfare Act

quiz.q: Approximately how much is Berlin's Hundesteuer (dog tax) per dog per year?
quiz.explanation: Berlin charges approximately €120/year Hundesteuer per dog — one of Germany's highest dog tax rates — with dangerous breed owners also required to hold €1m liability insurance.

laws.title: Insolvenzrecht — Bankruptcy in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Insolvency proceedings follow federal InsO; Berlin hosts a major Insolvenzgericht
laws.fullDescription: Insolvency in Germany is governed by the federal Insolvenzordnung (InsO). Debtors who are unable to pay their debts must file for insolvency immediately — directors of GmbH/AG companies have a maximum 3-week delay before mandatory filing (§15a InsO); breach is criminal. Berlin's Insolvenzgericht (at Amtsgericht Charlottenburg) handles a high volume of cases given Berlin's large corporate sector. Private individuals can file for Verbraucherinsolvenz (consumer insolvency) and obtain Restschuldbefreiung (discharge of remaining debts) after 3 years of good conduct. Berlin has some of Germany's highest business insolvency rates.
laws.penalty: Delayed or failed insolvency filing by director: up to 3 years imprisonment under §15a InsO; fraudulent concealment of assets: criminal charges
exceptions: Start-ups under 3 years old have modified insolvency pre-warning provisions
Small sole traders below certain thresholds have simplified Verbraucherinsolvenz pathway
laws.sourceLabel: German Insolvency Act / Civil Procedure Code

quiz.q: After how many years can a private individual in Germany receive Restschuldbefreiung (debt discharge) in insolvency?
quiz.explanation: Since 2021, German debtors can receive Restschuldbefreiung (discharge of remaining debts) after just 3 years of good conduct in insolvency — reduced from the previous 6 years.

laws.title: Olympiastadion Berlin — Heritage and Event Law
laws.subtitle: The 1936 Olympic Stadium is a protected monument hosting major events
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's Olympiastadion (Olympic Stadium), built for the 1936 Summer Olympics under the Nazi regime, is a protected monument (Baudenkmal) under DSchG Bln and a UNESCO Cultural Heritage site. It is home to Hertha BSC (Bundesliga football) and hosts major concerts and events including the DFB-Pokalfinale (German Cup Final). The stadium underwent a comprehensive renovation (2000–2004) while maintaining its listed facade. Events require comprehensive Veranstaltungsgenehmigung (event permits) covering safety, noise, transport, and crowd management. The stadium holds 74,475 spectators.
laws.penalty: Structural modifications without Denkmalschutzbehörde approval: fines up to €500,000; event safety violations: operational liability and criminal charges
exceptions: Temporary internal structures for concerts do not constitute permanent structural change
Maintenance and restoration by heritage-approved contractors
laws.sourceLabel: Berlin Monument Protection Act / Assembly Venue Ordinance

quiz.q: For which major event was Berlin's Olympiastadion originally built?
quiz.explanation: Berlin's Olympiastadion was built for the 1936 Summer Olympics, hosted under the Nazi regime — it is now a protected monument and active sports/events venue.

laws.title: Homeoffice-Recht — Remote Work Law in Berlin
laws.subtitle: No legal right to home office in Germany, but Berlin encourages flexible work
laws.fullDescription: Germany does not yet have a statutory right to Homeoffice (remote work), unlike some EU countries. Berlin employers may offer home office arrangements voluntarily. During the COVID-19 pandemic, federal SARS-CoV-2-Arbeitsschutzverordnung temporarily mandated home office offers where possible. The Arbeitsstättenverordnung (ArbStättV) and Bildschirmarbeitsverordnung require that home office workplaces meet basic ergonomic and safety standards if the employer establishes them. DSGVO/GDPR compliance requires secure data handling from home. The EU Platform Work Directive may affect flexible work classification.
laws.penalty: Employer-established home office failing ArbStättV standards: safety enforcement; GDPR violations in remote work context: fines
exceptions: Voluntary home office by employee choice with employer agreement may have reduced formal requirements
Emergency home office during crisis events treated with regulatory flexibility
laws.sourceLabel: Workplace Ordinance / Data Protection Act / Occupational Safety Act

quiz.q: Does Germany have a statutory right to work from home (Homeoffice)?
options: No — home office is voluntary; no legal right to demand it
Yes — introduced during COVID and made permanent
quiz.explanation: Germany does not have a statutory right to Homeoffice. Employers may offer it voluntarily, and ergonomics/safety rules apply to formally established home workplaces, but no legal entitlement exists.

laws.title: Wasserstraßen — Berlin's Inland Waterways
laws.subtitle: Berlin's 190 km of waterways are federal waterways; navigation rules apply
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's approximately 190 km of navigable waterways — including the Spree, Havel, and the Teltow Canal — are federal waterways (Bundeswasserstraßen) regulated by the Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsamt (WSA) Berlin-Spree-Havel. Boat operators must hold the Sportbootführerschein (inland waterways licence) for motorised vessels over 15 kW. Speed limits are 6–12 km/h in most areas to protect riverbanks from erosion. All vessels must be registered. The crossing of designated Schutzgebiete (protected areas) is restricted. Berlin's commercial ferry lines (Fähren) operate as public transport under BVG management.
laws.penalty: Operating without Sportbootführerschein: fines up to €1,500; exceeding speed limits: fines; unauthorized use of protected zones: fines up to €5,000
exceptions: Non-motorised craft (kayaks, rowing boats) under 15 kW do not require licence
Emergency rescue boats exempt from speed limits
laws.sourceLabel: Waterways Act / Inland Navigation Ordinance / Waterways Licence Ordinance

quiz.q: What licence is required for motorised vessels over 15 kW on Berlin's waterways?
quiz.explanation: The Sportbootführerschein Binnen (inland waterways licence) is required for motorised boats over 15 kW on Berlin's federal waterways — including the Spree and Havel.

laws.title: Stadtentwicklung — Berlin Urban Development Law
laws.subtitle: Berlin's FNP and Bebauungspläne govern all land use across the city
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's land use is governed by the Flächennutzungsplan (FNP Berlin, 1994, regularly updated) — the master plan designating land use for the entire city. Individual Bebauungspläne (B-Plans) set binding rules for specific areas. The Senatsverwaltung für Stadtentwicklung und Wohnen prepares major plans; Bezirke implement at district level. Berlin's Stadtentwicklungsplan (StEP) addresses specific themes including housing, mobility, and climate. The Liegenschaftsfonds Berlin manages state-owned properties. Major development projects require Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung (environmental impact assessment).
laws.penalty: Development contrary to Bebauungsplan: stop-work order and fines; unauthorized change of land use: administrative enforcement
exceptions: Befreiung (planning exemption) may be granted for minor deviations if basic principles not violated
Emergency demolition of unsafe structures permitted without full planning process
laws.sourceLabel: Federal Building Code / Berlin Land Use Plan / Berlin Building Code

quiz.q: What is Berlin's Flächennutzungsplan (FNP)?
options: The master land use plan designating uses across the entire city
quiz.explanation: The Flächennutzungsplan (FNP) is Berlin's master land use plan — designating which areas may be used for housing, commerce, industry, recreation and infrastructure across the whole city.

laws.title: Apothekenrecht — Pharmacy Law in Berlin
laws.subtitle: Prescription drugs require a Rezept; internet pharmacies must be EU-registered
laws.fullDescription: Berlin's pharmacies (Apotheken) operate under the federal Apothekengesetz (ApoG) and Apothekenbetriebsordnung (ApBetrO). Prescription-only drugs (Rx/Verschreibungspflichtig) may only be dispensed with a valid Rezept (prescription) from a licensed doctor. Over-the-counter drugs (OTC/Freiverkäuflich) are available in pharmacies and, for some products, in supermarkets. Online pharmacies must be registered with the EU-wide safety logo (EU-Sicherheitslogo). Berlin has approximately 900 pharmacies. Emergency pharmacies (Notdienstapotheken) maintain 24/7 cover on a rotating basis.
laws.penalty: Dispensing prescription drugs without prescription: criminal charges under BtMG or ApoG; operating unlicensed pharmacy: immediate closure and criminal charges
exceptions: Doctors treating patients may provide medication directly in emergency
Veterinary medicines dispensed by licensed veterinarians
laws.sourceLabel: Pharmacy Act / Pharmacy Operations Ordinance / Narcotics Act

quiz.q: What must an online pharmacy operating in Germany display to prove it is legally registered?
options: A Federal Association of German Pharmacists seal
quiz.explanation: All legally registered online pharmacies selling to German customers must display the EU-Sicherheitslogo (EU safety logo) — a clickable badge verifying registration with the relevant national authority.

laws.title: Staatsoper Berlin — Opera and Performance Law
laws.subtitle: The Staatsoper Unter den Linden is state-funded; performance rights governed by UrhG
laws.fullDescription: The Staatsoper Unter den Linden (Berlin State Opera) is one of three state-funded opera houses in Berlin (alongside the Komische Oper and the Deutsche Oper). Together they receive approximately €130 million in annual public subsidy. Performances must comply with the Urheberrechtsgesetz (UrhG — copyright law), with GEMA and VG Bild-Kunst collecting royalties for living composers and rights holders. The Intendant (director) is appointed by the Senatsverwaltung für Kultur. The Staatsoper building (rebuilt, reopened 2017) is a protected monument.
laws.penalty: Unauthorised commercial recording of performances: civil damages under UrhG; violation of performers' rights: injunctions and compensation
exceptions: Personal non-commercial video clips (brief) generally tolerated
Press photography with accreditation permitted during designated portions
laws.sourceLabel: Copyright Act / GEMA / Artists Copyright Act

quiz.q: How many state-funded opera houses does Berlin have?
quiz.explanation: Berlin has three state-funded opera houses: the Staatsoper Unter den Linden, the Komische Oper, and the Deutsche Oper — collectively receiving approximately €130 million in annual public subsidy.

laws.title: Außenwirtschaftsrecht — Foreign Trade and Investment Screening
laws.subtitle: Foreign investment in German critical infrastructure requires federal approval
laws.fullDescription: While trade policy is EU competence, Germany's Außenwirtschaftsgesetz (AWG) and Außenwirtschaftsverordnung (AWV) allow the federal government to screen and block foreign direct investments that threaten security or public order. Berlin, as Germany's startup hub and home to critical federal infrastructure, is a sensitive location. Acquisitions of 10%+ stakes in defence, critical infrastructure, or media companies require notification to BMWi (Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft). Several Chinese acquisition attempts of Berlin-based companies have been blocked under AWG review. EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation (2023) adds additional screening for subsidised foreign entities.
laws.penalty: Completing notifiable transaction without approval: transaction may be unwound; criminal penalties for deliberate circumvention
exceptions: Investments within the EU/EEA are not subject to foreign investment screening
Portfolio investments below notification thresholds freely permitted
laws.sourceLabel: German Foreign Trade Act / Foreign Trade Ordinance / EU FDI Screening Regulation

quiz.q: What ownership stake in a German critical infrastructure company triggers foreign investment review?
quiz.explanation: Under Germany's AWV, acquisitions of 10% or more of voting rights in critical infrastructure, defence, or media companies require notification to the federal government for security screening.
